newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pechiney to begin job cuts in June - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pechiney to begin job cuts in June - paper.

text.p: Pechiney's chairman Jean-Pierre Rodier said on Friday during a visit to Brazil the French aluminium company plans to start cutting jobs in France in June this year, according to French newspaper reports on Saturday.
Le Figaro said Rodier did not specify the number of jobs to go nor which factories were concerned but the paper said by using various measures outright redundancies would be avoided.
Both papers said unions had reacted angrily to the news on Friday, strongly condemning the methods used by the Pechiney management.
No company officials were immediately available for comment.

Out of a total of 5,000 job cuts planned worldwide, part of Pechiney's Challenge cost-cutting plan unveiled in September last year, some 2,700 jobs will be lost in France, Liberation and Le Figaro said.
The plan aims to make savings of four billion francs during a three year period. ((-- Paris Newsroom +331 4221 5542))
